authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In this development and validation case, the defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was lower than the plain attack branch. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack clean reference, without establishing oracle clean recovery.

facts.statement: The selected coalition was B_hash_ranked with 10 clients and an exact poison pair; the source class was DDoS and the target class was Benign.
The plain mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.185175, compared with 0.083392 for the defended branch and 0.077628 for the paired clean branch.
The defended branch reduced the DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate by 0.101783 relative to the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and mean and maximum benign false-positive rate were 0.000000.

interpretations.statement: Observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward Benign, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: the supplied evidence does not verify it.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and was not substituted.
Refuse to make client flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is a paired round-4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
The evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
